text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pensions will not be reduced, said labour and social policy minister Naser Ziberi. The government has no right to make restrictions on already set pensions.
- Macedonia should become aware of its drug problem and mount a real fight against abuse, smuggling and illegal production of narcotics, the parliament said at its session.
- Opposition ethnic Albanian parties PDPA and NDP are considering integration into a single party.
- Parliamentary opposition Liberal Democratic Party claims the government is selling flats to ruling SDAM deputies, ministers and judges at extremely low prices providing a list of names.

- Macedonian Foreign Minister Blagoj Handziski will remain firm in the stand that the name Republic of Macedonia should be kept for international use while a name should be agreed upon for bilateral use during his June meeting in Athens with his Greek counterpart Theodoros Pangalos. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
